title: frozen-comparand lint has no quote awareness: it flags `-eq N` inside quoted test-input strings and grep search patterns, making it impossible to author behavioral oracles for the rule itself
description:
MEASURED LIVE, and it deterministically blocked a real plan twice, escalating it.

While planning CAM-382 (widening the frozen-comparand rule), the deterministic oracle lint at src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1036 blocked BOTH re-plan rounds and wrote .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json with roundsCompleted:2. All THREE findings are FALSE POSITIVES. Verbatim from the escalation marker:

  1. bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const cs=["test $X -eq 41","test $X -ge 41","test $X -le 41","test $X == 41"];for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)===null){...}}'
  2. bun -e '...const cs=["cmd --ge 5","echo foo-eq 42"];for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)!==null){...}}'
  3. grep -qF 'test $(git grep -c PATTERN mainbranch:file.ts) -eq 1' test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts

In (1) and (2) the `-eq 41` / `--ge 5` are TEST INPUT DATA inside a quoted JS array, passed to rule.test() by a behavioral oracle. In (3) the `-eq 1` is the SEARCH PATTERN of a grep -qF, i.e. the literal text being looked for in a test file. None of the three is a shell comparison at all.

ROOT CAUSE: hasFrozenIntegerComparand (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:168-171) applies INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE to the WHOLE command string as a flat regex. It has no notion of shell quoting, no tokenization, and no awareness that a match may sit inside a single-quoted, double-quoted, or nested string literal. Any occurrence of the operator+integer byte pattern anywhere in the command trips it.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A GENERIC FALSE POSITIVE: it is SELF-REFERENTIAL. The natural way to write a falsifiable acceptance oracle for a rule that classifies shell comparisons is to feed it example shell comparisons and assert the classification. That oracle necessarily embeds comparison-shaped strings as data. So the rule structurally forbids behavioral oracles about itself, which is exactly the oracle style patterns.md and the project convention otherwise push authors toward. Any future story touching this rule hits the same wall.

It also false-positives well beyond this module: ANY oracle that greps for text containing a comparison (`grep -qF 'test ... -eq 1' somefile`) is flagged, which is a common and legitimate way to pin that a test file contains a specific assertion.

DIRECTION (needs a real decision, do not headless-implement): make the scan quote-aware, so a match inside a quoted string literal is not treated as a live comparison. Options worth weighing: strip or skip single/double-quoted spans before scanning; require the comparison to sit in shell command position; or add an explicit authoring escape hatch. Note that stripping quoted spans would also weaken genuine detection for oracles that legitimately quote their whole test expression, so this is a real trade-off, not a one-liner. Whatever is chosen must keep the rule catching the CAM-377 shape it exists for.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER ISSUES: CAM-383 is the OPPOSITE error (over-EXCUSING: any derivation token anywhere excuses every comparand). This is over-FLAGGING. CAM-382 (widening the operator alternation to -gt/-lt/-ne/!=) will make this STRICTLY WORSE, since more operators means more byte patterns that can appear inside quoted data. CAM-386 is a third axis (what counts as a derivation token). All four live in the same ~30 lines. Sequencing matters: shipping CAM-382 without this fix makes the self-referential trap harder to escape.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY: this is not theoretical. It cost a full plan phase plus two re-plan rounds and left .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json on disk. The lint runs BEFORE the auditor is ever spawned, so a false positive here burns the whole planning cycle with no auditor judgment applied.

Needs rebuild: prd-oracle-lint.ts is sidecar-executed at plan time.

spec.scope: Make the frozen-comparand oracle-lint rule quote-aware, so an operator+integer byte pattern sitting inside a single- or double-quoted span of an oracle command is not mistaken for a live shell comparison. ROOT CAUSE: hasFrozenIntegerComparand (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:164-171) applies INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE and LIVE_DERIVATION_RE to the flat whole command string with no shell tokenization and no quote state, so quoted test-input data and grep search patterns trip it. DIRECTION CHOSEN, on measurement not taste: strip quoted spans before scanning, with `-c '<payload>'` wrapper payloads UNWRAPPED (recursed into) rather than deleted, so `sh -c 'test $(wc -l < f) -eq 3'` keeps flagging. The competing directions were measured and rejected: requiring shell command position needs a real tokenizer, which the module's own header comment (:89-91) deliberately forbids, and it still fails the quoted-JS-payload case without also doing quote tracking; an authoring escape hatch would make self-referential oracles authorable but permanently unlinted, which does not restore the rule's coverage of its own domain. TRADE-OFF MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the feared regression is that stripping quotes weakens detection for oracles that legitimately quote their whole test expression. Measured across the repo's entire real oracle history (226 unique [oracle:] directives in scripts/cam and .claude): current and quote-stripped predicates agree 226/226. All 14 existing frozen-comparand test inputs keep their verdicts. The CAM-377 shape the rule exists for stays flagged. The sole regressing shape is `sh -c '<comparison>'`, which has zero instances in the repo today and is closed anyway by the unwrapping requirement. STRICTLY OUT OF SCOPE, do not touch: (a) the missing LEFT word boundary on INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE, which makes bare `foo-eq 42` and `cmd --ge 5` flag; that is a distinct defect already specified in CAM-382 and must stay there. (b) Widening the operator alternation to -gt/-lt/-ne/!= (CAM-382). (c) LIVE_DERIVATION_RE's \bmain\b matching the 'main' inside filenames (CAM-386). (d) The over-excusing behavior where any derivation token anywhere excuses every comparand (CAM-383). (e) ROTATING_ARTIFACT_RULE, whose quote-blindness is INTENTIONAL and documented verbatim in its own doc comment at :209-211; it must not be routed through the new stripping helper. The other two rules (grep-q-plus-list-files, zero-match-vacuous) share the same latent quote-blind class but have no measured incident and are out of scope. Module purity is a load-bearing journaled invariant: no I/O may be introduced, and lintStoryCriteria and lintPrd must stay behaviorally unchanged. Needs rebuild after merge: prd-oracle-lint.ts is sidecar-executed at plan time. RED-SWEEP RECORD, measured against unmodified main before dispatch, exhaustive not sampled: AC1 and AC3 are BEHAVIORALLY RED (AC1 produces 3 real misclassifications against a 7-row fixture while correctly classifying the other 4, so it is non-vacuous in both directions; AC3 replays the 3 verbatim commands from the live escalation marker and all 3 are wrongly flagged on main). AC2 and AC5 are FIXTURE-SHAPE GUARDS that go green the moment the fixture exists, and are labelled as such rather than laundered as red. AC4, AC6, AC7 and AC8 are deliberately GREEN pinning criteria and are labelled as such. No criterion is claimed red that was not observed red.
acceptanceCriteria: A data-driven behavioral fixture of oracle-lint cases exists (format: <ruleName> :: <ok|flag> :: <command>) and EVERY case classifies as its recorded expectation, covering both directions: quoted-span cases that must NOT flag, and genuine live comparisons that MUST still flag. [oracle: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const rows=(await Bun.file("test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt").text()).trim().split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(l=>l&&!l.startsWith("#")).map(l=>l.split(" :: "));if(!rows.length){console.log("VACUOUS: no rows");process.exit(1)}let bad=0;for(const [rn,want,cmd] of rows){const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name===rn);if(!r){console.log("NO SUCH RULE "+rn);bad++;continue}const got=r.test(cmd)?"flag":"ok";if(got!==want){console.log("MISMATCH rule="+rn+" want="+want+" got="+got+" cmd="+cmd);bad++}}console.log("rows="+rows.length+" bad="+bad);process.exit(bad?1:0)']

FIXTURE-SHAPE GUARD, not behaviorally red on main (it goes green as soon as the fixture exists; its job is to stop the fixture from being narrowed into vacuity): The fixture is non-vacuous in both directions for frozen-comparand, carrying at least one case of each of four required shapes: a quoted test-input payload expected ok, a grep search pattern expected ok, a bare live comparison expected flag, and a -c wrapper payload expected flag. [oracle: bun -e 'const rows=(await Bun.file("test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt").text()).trim().split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(l=>l&&!l.startsWith("#")).map(l=>l.split(" :: "));const f=rows.filter(r=>r[0]==="frozen-comparand");const ok=f.filter(r=>r[1]==="ok").length;const flag=f.filter(r=>r[1]==="flag").length;const wrapped=f.filter(r=>r[1]==="flag"&&r[2].includes(" -c ")).length;const grepPat=f.filter(r=>r[1]==="ok"&&r[2].includes("grep")).length;console.log({rows:rows.length,ok,flag,wrapped,grepPat});process.exit(ok&&flag&&wrapped&&grepPat?0:1)']

All three oracle commands recorded verbatim in the live escalation marker .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json (the real CAM-382 incident, all three false positives) are classified ok by the fixed rule. [oracle: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const m=await Bun.file(".claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json").json();const cmds=m.findings.map(f=>{const s=f.description.indexOf("oracle command `");const e=f.description.lastIndexOf("`: oracle compares");return f.description.slice(s+16,e)});if(cmds.length!==m.findings.length||!cmds.length)process.exit(1);let bad=0;for(const c of cmds){if(r.test(c)!==null){console.log("STILL FLAGGED:",c);bad++}}process.exit(bad?1:0)']

PINNING CRITERION, deliberately GREEN on main and not red-swept: The rule still flags the CAM-377 shape it exists for, re-derived live from the patterns.md bullet that records it rather than frozen as a literal. [oracle: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const c="test $(grep -c handoff.json scripts/cam/patterns.md) -eq "+String(Bun.spawnSync(["grep","-c","handoff.json","scripts/cam/patterns.md"]).stdout.toString().trim());process.exit(r.test(c)?0:1)']

FIXTURE-SHAPE GUARD, not behaviorally red on main (it goes green as soon as the fixture exists; its job is to stop the fixture from being narrowed into vacuity): ROTATING_ARTIFACT_RULE is NOT routed through the new quote-stripping helper: the fixture carries at least one rotating-artifact-target case whose rotating path sits inside quotes, and it still flags, preserving that rule's documented intentional quote-blindness. [oracle: bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const rows=(await Bun.file("test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt").text()).trim().split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter(l=>l&&!l.startsWith("#")).map(l=>l.split(" :: "));const q=rows.filter(r=>r[0]==="rotating-artifact-target"&&r[1]==="flag"&&(r[2].includes(String.fromCharCode(39))||r[2].includes(String.fromCharCode(34))));console.log("quoted rotating cases="+q.length);if(!q.length)process.exit(1);const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="rotating-artifact-target");process.exit(q.every(x=>r.test(x[2])!==null)?0:1)']

PINNING CRITERION, deliberately GREEN on main and not red-swept: module purity is preserved, no I/O import or call is introduced into the lint module. [oracle: bash -c '! grep -qE "node:fs|node:child_process|from .node:|Bun\\.spawn|Bun\\.file|readFileSync" src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts']

PINNING CRITERION, deliberately GREEN on main and not red-swept: The public surface of lintPrd and lintStoryCriteria is unchanged: the full existing test file passes with no test removed, and the total test count does not drop below main's, re-derived live rather than frozen. [oracle: bash -c 'bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts']
Full quality spine is green: bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all all pass. [oracle: bash -c 'bun run typecheck && bun run check:all']
gotchas: SELF-REFERENTIAL TRAP, READ FIRST: this rule classifies shell comparisons, so any behavioral oracle about it must embed comparison-shaped strings as DATA. That is exactly what the unfixed rule false-positives on, and it is why this issue's own plan escalated twice. The acceptance oracles above deliberately keep the operator+integer literals OUT of the oracle command by loading them from test/fixtures/oracle-lint/frozen-comparand-cases.txt. This is data relocation, not oracle weakening: the behavioral assertion is identical in strength, and the fixture is legitimate data-driven test design. Do NOT 'simplify' by inlining the cases back into the oracle command; that will re-trip the lint and re-escalate the plan.

Do NOT obfuscate operator literals via string concatenation to dodge the lint. That is gate-gaming. If a needed oracle cannot be authored without tripping the unfixed rule, HALT and report rather than working around it.

ROTATING_ARTIFACT_RULE's quote-blindness is INTENTIONAL and is stated verbatim in its doc comment at src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:209-211, with a test at :266 asserting the quoted case flags. Routing it through the new stripping helper will break that test and is a correctness regression, not a cleanup.

The module is PURE with exactly two imports (parseOracleDirectives from ./behavioral-gate.ts, and a type-only PrdShape from ../commands/status.ts). Its header comment at :30-31 declares 'Pure, no I/O', and journal.md:517 records that CAM-381 preserved it. Do not add I/O to build the fixture reader; the fixture is read by the TEST and by the acceptance oracle, never by the lint module itself.

hasFrozenIntegerComparand applies TWO regexes. Both must see the same stripped text, or a derivation token that legitimately lives inside quotes would stop excusing a comparand and you would trade an over-flagging bug for an over-excusing one (which is CAM-383's separate defect). Strip once, test both against the stripped string.

The `-c` unwrapping requirement is what keeps `sh -c 'test $(wc -l < f) -eq 3'` flagged. Naive deletion of quoted spans makes that shape silently pass. Measured population of that shape in the repo today is zero, so no existing oracle regresses either way, but the requirement closes the hole before CAM-382 widens the operator set and enlarges it.

The lint runs at src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1036, BEFORE resolveAndSpawnAuditor is ever called, and MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS is 2 (plan-runner.ts:102). A false positive therefore burns an entire planning cycle with zero auditor judgment applied. This is why the fix is worth more than its diff size.

biome enforces cognitive complexity; if the stripping helper plus the two regex tests push hasFrozenIntegerComparand over the threshold, extract the stripper as its own named module-local function rather than inlining it.
NEEDS REBUILD after merge: prd-oracle-lint.ts is executed by the sidecar at plan time, so the fix has no effect until the binary is rebuilt and the sidecar respawned.
domainTerms: frozen comparand: an acceptance-criterion oracle that compares against a literal integer read off main at authoring time instead of re-deriving it at check time, so it rots silently when a later commit edits the compared file.
quote blindness: applying a shell-shaped regex to a whole command string with no quote state, so a byte pattern inside a quoted string literal is misread as live shell syntax.

self-referential oracle trap: the condition where a lint rule's own domain is shell text, so any falsifiable behavioral oracle about the rule must embed that text as data and is then flagged by the rule itself.

oracle lint: the deterministic pre-auditor scan (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts, CAM-310/CAM-381) that walks a freshly generated PRD's acceptance-criterion oracle commands against a named-rules list and blocks the plan round on any finding.
